heading: Nominee vs Legal Heir: Who Gets Your Investments Without a Will?
tldr: A nominee is primarily a custodian or facilitator appointed by the investor to receive assets upon their death.
Without a valid Will, the legal heirs, as per applicable succession laws, are generally the true owners of the deceased's assets.
For bank fixed deposits and mutual funds, the nominee typically acts as a trustee, holding the assets on behalf of the legal heirs.
In the case of Public Provident Fund (PPF), the nominee can sometimes be the beneficial owner, depending on specific rules and the absence of a Will.
Creating a comprehensive Will is crucial as it overrides nominations and ensures your assets are distributed exactly as you intend.
caption:
Ever wondered who truly gets your money after you're gone if you don't have a Will? It's a common confusion! While you might name a nominee for your investments, they don't always become the final owner. Often, a nominee just holds the money until your legal heirs are decided. This article clears up who gets what, especially for FDs, MFs, and PPF. Don't leave your loved ones guessing. Read more to understand this important difference.
